properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Simulator fixtures: ten ssl_certs_N.py modules each embed a full TLS PKI (CA key + per-service RSA-2048 keys and certs) as byte literals, used by chia_full_node_simulator to bring up local test networks without generating certificates. They ship in the wheel but are intended for throwaway local simulators only; real deployments generate their own CA via chia/ssl/create_ssl.py. Changeable here (runtime generation), though the simulator explicitly wants deterministic fixtures.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Mutual-TLS node authentication: peers are identified by certificate + pinned CA (chia's own CA), not by DNS name — node certs carry SAN=chia.net but services dial by IP/port, so hostname checking is off by design while verify_mode=CERT_REQUIRED keeps chain verification on. Posture control recorded; changeable here but the alternative (hostnames in SANs) is a fleet-wide migration.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Availability-only: pycryptodome 3.23.0 ships 3DES (TripleDES module) and is a transitive dependency (pulled by keyrings-cryptfile, the legacy OS-fallback keyring backend). No Crypto/Cryptodome import exists anywhere in chia's code, so no 3DES call site. Presence is the inventory fact; the legacy keyring path is the only reachable consumer.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Breakdown: the overwhelming majority are assert/if equality checks in _tests and benchmarks comparing PUBLIC consensus identifiers (header_hash, puzzle_hash, challenge_hash) — timing-irrelevant. Production sites compare locally entered passphrases (cmds/passphrase_funcs.py), CLVM cost counters, and the public CHECKBYTES canary in file_keyring.py; no MAC or signature verification happens in this codebase's own comparisons — BLS verification and Poly1305 tags are checked inside chia_rs and cryptog

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Breakdown: benchmark/test data generation (random.Random/randint/randbytes) and non-security production uses — peer selection jitter (introducer, node_discovery, address_manager), wallet coin selection, seeder crawl ordering. No key, nonce, seed or token generation uses the non-crypto PRNG; wallet entropy comes from BIP39 mnemonics and the OS CSPRNG (secrets/os.urandom). Real pattern, correct usage — kept as a posture record.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Two PBKDF2 sites with different stories: file_keyring.py:52 derives the keyring encryption key with PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 at 100,000 iterations (HASH_ITERS) — below OWASP's 600,000 recommendation for SHA-256, protecting wallet private keys at rest; changeable here. keychain.py:163 is the BIP39 mnemonic-to-seed derivation at the spec-fixed 2048 iterations of PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA512 — interoperability-mandated, not changeable unilaterally.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: The Poly1305 one-time authenticator inside the ChaCha20Poly1305 AEAD securing the keyring file (master passphrase-derived key). Its tag comparison happens inside the cryptography library, not in this code; the CHECKBYTES_VALUE != comparison at line 60 is a public canary, not the MAC.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: The complete explicit cipher list for the TLS 1.2 downgrade path: ten suites, every one ECDHE (secp256r1-class NIST curves via OpenSSL defaults) — zero post-quantum or hybrid groups. Harvest-now-decrypt-later applies to daemon RPC traffic when the downgrade is enabled. Changeable here.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: ECDSA appears only as the authentication signature inside the daemon's TLS 1.2 downgrade cipher list (chia's own certs are RSA; ECDHE-ECDSA suites would apply to ECDSA peer certs). Plus availability via the cryptography dependency.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: All inter-service Chia traffic (full_node/wallet/farmer/harvester/daemon) runs over mutual TLS with the local chia CA: every context loads a service cert and requires peer certs. Changeable here (crypto agility decided by the Python ssl module / linked OpenSSL).

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: The floor for all node-to-node and daemon TLS is TLS 1.3 — good: it's the only TLS version with a PQ migration path (hybrid X25519MLKEM768 key share). Whether the hybrid group is actually offered depends on the linked OpenSSL version, unknown here.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Config-gated TLS downgrade: daemon_allow_tls_1_2 (default false) relaxes the daemon's TLS floor to 1.2 AND replaces the default suite list with an explicit classical-only ECDHE list (no PQ groups exist in TLS 1.2). Changeable here: remove the option or refuse the downgrade.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Vendored Mozilla CA bundle (chia/ssl/cacert.pem, get_mozilla_ca_crt) shipped for outbound HTTPS trust. Some included CA certificates use P-384/P-521 EC keys — Shor-relevant the day large quantum computers exist, but observable here and replaceable only by Mozilla upstream. Also covers the 254 content-identified certificates already in the inventory.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: SHA-3-256 (keccak) enters Chia via the Chialisp "keccak" softfork operator (op 62, softfork 1134): test_mempool.py constructs programs exercising the operator and hashes announcements with sha3. Consensus-track algorithm — Grover-only risk, no Shor impact; changeable only by softfork.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: SHA-256 is the consensus hashing spine of Chia: Chialisp puzzle/coin tree hashing (load_clvm.py, p2_delegated puzzle synthetic-pk hashing), wallet merkle utilities, and std_hash (chia/util/hash.py wraps hashlib.sha256, used in hundreds of call sites across the repo). Grover-only risk — 256-bit output keeps an effective 128-bit security level. Not a migration priority; changeable only by consensus hard fork.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: AES-128-GCM suites in the daemon's explicit TLS 1.2 downgrade cipher list (only active when daemon_allow_tls_1_2=true). Symmetric layer is fine; the KEX in front of it is the quantum risk.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: AES ships in two locked providers: pycryptodome 3.23.0 (transitive via keyrings-cryptfile, which encrypts its keyring file with AES) and pyca/cryptography 50.0.1 (the app's own provider, though the file keyring itself uses ChaCha20Poly1305). Availability inventory; no direct AES call site in chia code.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: PBKDF2 is the only KDF in the key-management path: passphrase->keyring key (file_keyring.py) and mnemonic->wallet seed (BIP39, keychain.py). Same two sites as the low-iterations object; both live.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: npm lockfile integrity digests (sha256- prefixed base64) for the build_scripts installer dependencies — supply-chain integrity checking, not authentication of secrets. Grover-only risk. Dependency inventory for the shipped Node bundle.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: npm lockfile integrity digests (blake3- prefixed) — newer npm may record BLAKE3 digests alongside sha512. Supply-chain integrity checking only; BLAKE3 is Grover-resistant at 256-bit output. Dependency inventory for the shipped Node bundle.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: npm lockfile integrity digests (sha3-256): supply-chain integrity checking for installer dependencies. Grover-only risk. Same lockfile inventory as the SHA-256/BLAKE3 entries.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Availability-only: argon2-cffi is locked in poetry.lock but no argon2 import exists in chia's code — the app's password KDFs are PBKDF2 (file keyring) and BIP39. A future keyring hardening would use this dependency; its presence is the inventory fact.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: AES-256 suites in the daemon's explicit TLS 1.2 downgrade cipher list; also the AEAD strength class for the file keyring. Symmetric ciphers are Grover-only risks; the ECDHE key exchange ahead of them is the migration driver.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Two distinct uses: (1) ECDHE-*-CHACHA20-POLY1305 suites in the daemon TLS 1.2 downgrade cipher list; (2) the ChaCha20Poly1305 AEAD that encrypts the on-disk keyring file (chia/util/file_keyring.py encrypt_data/decrypt_data) — the file holding wallet private keys, keyed by PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 from the user passphrase. AEAD is Grover-only; the passphrase KDF is the weaker link. Changeable here.

components.name: Python ssl sessions on default settings (OpenSSL version unknown)

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Every outbound HTTPS client in the node (RPC client, data-layer S3/download, farmer pool links, plot-NFT pool checks, daemon client, dev_gh test helper) runs on stock ssl defaults — no explicit group or suite lists anywhere, so key-exchange agility is decided entirely by the interpreter's linked OpenSSL: ≥3.5 offers X25519MLKEM768 hybrid by default; earlier versions are classical-only and harvestable. Version is not pinned in this repo (system Python).

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: The root context (ssl_context_for_root) is the one context Chia creates with factory defaults: ssl.create_default_context(purpose=SERVER_AUTH, cafile=chia_ca) — default protocol versions and groups, only the trust store is pinned. Whether a hybrid X25519MLKEM768 group gets offered depends on the runtime OpenSSL, which this repo does not pin. The poetry.lock sites are TLS availability via the cryptography/urllib3/requests stack.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: The CSPRNG choice is correct: secrets/os.urandom (OS CSPRNG) is used for the one production randomness need in the scanned paths (unique in-memory sqlite DB names) and test keys. Quantum-safe; no finding. Wallet entropy itself comes from the BIP39 mnemonic (keychain.py), not from these calls.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: X.509 certificate handling is how Chia derives node identities: calculate_node_id (server.py) loads the peer's PEM cert, re-encodes DER, and takes the SHA-256 fingerprint as the node ID used for connection authorization; tests load generated certs the same way. Changeable here.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: @noble/hashes is the npm crypto provider for the bundled installer scripts in build_scripts/npm_linux — ships SHA-2/SHA-3/BLAKE/keccak primitives for the Node bundle. Availability inventory; no app call site in Python code.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: certifi provides the Mozilla CA bundle for the requests/urllib3 HTTPS stack (outbound RPC/pool-service calls). Trust-store governance: rotation follows certifi releases; replaceable by vendor upgrade.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: X.509 machinery (parse/build/sign/serialize) ships in pyca/cryptography 50.0.1, consumed directly by chia/ssl/create_ssl.py (CA + node cert generation) and server.py (node-ID fingerprints). Same package as LIB-4eba82ef/LIB-dfb9c980.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: certifi is the trust-store provider feeding urllib3/requests verification for outbound HTTPS from the node; update cadence decides CA agility. Same purpose as ALG-065af532 (algorithm side).

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: urllib3 is the TLS transport under requests for outbound HTTPS (pool services, S3 data-layer downloads, dev checks); its default TLS behavior mirrors the PROTO-dca6de59 sessions — group choice is runtime-OpenSSL-decided.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: pycryptodome is a transitive dependency (via keyrings-cryptfile, the legacy OS-fallback file keyring backend chia/legacy/keyring.py can instantiate) — it is the AES/3DES provider for that backend. No direct import in chia code; availability-only.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: argon2-cffi locked but unused by application code — the keyring's passphrase KDF is PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 at 100k iterations (see ALG-a861135a). Availability-only entry; a natural upgrade path for the keyring KDF.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: requests carries the outbound HTTPS calls (pool service checks in plotnft_funcs, farmer pool state, data-layer fetches); TLS behavior is stock Python-ssl defaults over certifi's CA bundle.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: This is the same pyca/cryptography dependency as LIB-4eba82ef, recorded from the lockfile side: version 50.0.1 pinned in poetry.lock, provider of RSA/X.509/ChaCha20Poly1305 for the application.
